financials_interim.notes: Company (standalone parent) figures -- Mitsubishi/Fuso vehicles, spare parts, lubricants and hiring only; subsidiaries carry the Equipment & machinery, Tyres, 3D printers and Trailers segments and are excluded here. Same subtotal/identity checks as the GROUP row all tie out exactly: 484,277 + 17,068 - 17,229 = 484,116 (PBT), 484,116 - 136,693 = 347,423 (PAT), EPS 0.34 = 347,423k / 1,009,006,260 shares, and total_assets = total_liabilities + total_equity for both 30.06.2026 and 31.03.2026. long_term_borrowings = 0 (Company has no non-current interest bearing borrowings this period); short_term_borrowings = current interest bearing borrowings only (no Company-level bank overdraft disclosed).

Group figures. 'operating_profit' = filing's own 'Profit from operations' subtotal (after distribution/admin expenses, net impairment on receivables, other gains-net, and other income; before finance income/cost). Income statement, balance sheet and cash flow tables are internally consistent (no dual-rendering / column-swap artifact detected): operating_profit + finance_income - finance_costs = PBT exactly (1,306,213 + 23,893 - 179,928 = 1,150,178) for both current and prior columns, PBT - tax = PAT exactly for both columns, EPS (0.81) = PAT (815,946k) / shares in issue (1,009,006,260) ties out, and total_assets = total_liabilities + total_equity exactly for both 30.06.2026 and 31.03.2026. short_term_borrowings = current interest bearing borrowings (5,606,510) + bank overdrafts (221,924), both genuine interest-bearing debt; long_term_borrowings = non-current interest bearing borrowings only (4,460). trade_receivables = 'Trade and other receivables' line (5,823,801) as no separate trade-only figure is disclosed on the face of the SOFP. No NCI/minority interest -- 100% of profit and equity is attributable to owners of the parent, so minority_interest = 0. The SOFP in this filing compares 30.06.2026 (unaudited) only against 31.03.2026 (audited FYE), not against 30.06.2025, so there is no YoY balance-sheet comparative available from this filing -- only the P&L YoY comparison (vs the 30.06.2025 column in the income statement) is usable.

interim_updates.note_text: United Motors Lanka PLC's Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026) Group revenue more than doubled to LKR 13,526mn (+105.3% YoY, from LKR 6,587mn), driven overwhelmingly by the Vehicles segment: external revenue there rose from LKR 4,118mn to LKR 10,206mn (+147.8% YoY), accounting for LKR 6,088mn of the LKR 6,939mn total revenue increase, against an unusually weak Q1 FY2025/26 comparator. Vehicles segment profit rose in step, from LKR 449mn to LKR 1,117mn (+148.4%), and was the dominant driver of total segment profit growth from LKR 797mn to LKR 1,555mn. Lubricants and car care segment profit jumped from LKR 11.8mn to LKR 82.2mn (+596.8%), while Tyres segment profit fell from LKR 18.4mn to LKR 4.3mn (-76.6%) and Trailers profit slipped from LKR 134.3mn to LKR 130.1mn (-3.1%), partially offsetting the Vehicles-led gains. Group profit from operations rose 128.7% to LKR 1,306mn, but net finance cost widened from LKR 110mn to LKR 156mn (-41.6%) as finance income nearly halved (LKR 49.8mn to LKR 23.9mn, -52.0%) while finance cost rose 12.5% (LKR 160.0mn to LKR 179.9mn) -- this swing dampened, but did not reverse, the flow-through to PBT (+149.5% to LKR 1,150mn) and PAT (+159.5% to LKR 816mn). Unallocated (corporate) expenses rose 40.0% YoY (LKR 255mn to LKR 357mn). On a standalone Company basis (Mitsubishi/Fuso vehicles, spare parts, lubricants and hiring only), revenue grew 170.5% to LKR 6,121mn and PAT grew 210.5% to LKR 347mn, an even sharper swing than at Group level since the Company entity carries the core Vehicles franchise directly.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to this one has been collected for UML -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol. Additionally, the Statement of Financial Position in this filing compares 30.06.2026 (unaudited) only against 31.03.2026 (audited FYE), not against 30.06.2025, so no YoY balance-sheet comparison is available from this filing -- only P&L-based YoY comparisons (against the 30.06.2025 comparative column in the income statement) are included above.
interim_updates.takeaway: The headline 159.5% YoY PAT growth is almost entirely a Vehicles-segment story riding an unusually weak Q1 FY2025/26 comparator, not a broad-based margin improvement -- Tyres and Trailers segment profits actually fell YoY and Group net finance cost worsened 41.6% as finance income halved, so the YoY growth rate should be read as base-effect-driven rather than a sustainable new run-rate.
operational_highlights: Group revenue LKR 13,526mn, +105.3% YoY (Q1 FY2025/26: LKR 6,587mn)
Group profit for the period LKR 816mn, +159.5% YoY (Q1 FY2025/26: LKR 314mn); basic/diluted EPS LKR 0.81 vs LKR 0.31
Vehicles segment external revenue +147.8% YoY to LKR 10,206mn; segment profit +148.4% YoY to LKR 1,117mn
Group net finance cost widened to LKR 156mn from LKR 110mn (-41.6%) as finance income nearly halved (LKR 49.8mn to LKR 23.9mn, -52.0%)
Company (standalone) revenue LKR 6,121mn (+170.5% YoY) and PAT LKR 347mn (+210.5% YoY)
Group net assets per share LKR 17.82 at 30.06.2026 vs LKR 17.41 at 31.03.2026 (audited FYE, not a YoY comparative)
key_drivers: Vehicles segment (Mitsubishi/Fuso plus subsidiary brands) was the overwhelming growth driver: external revenue rose from LKR 4,118mn to LKR 10,206mn (+147.8% YoY) and segment profit rose from LKR 449mn to LKR 1,117mn (+148.4%), against a low Q1 FY2025/26 base.

Net finance cost widened 41.6% (LKR 110mn to LKR 156mn) as finance income fell 52.0% (LKR 49.8mn to LKR 23.9mn) while finance cost rose 12.5% (LKR 160.0mn to LKR 179.9mn), a swing that dampened -- but did not reverse -- the flow-through from the 128.7% rise in profit from operations to the 149.5% rise in PBT.
Tyres segment profit fell 76.6% (LKR 18.4mn to LKR 4.3mn) and Trailers profit slipped 3.1% (LKR 134.3mn to LKR 130.1mn), partially offsetting the Vehicles-led gains.
Unallocated (corporate) expenses rose 40.0% YoY (LKR 255mn to LKR 357mn), only partly offset by a LKR 79mn rise in unallocated other income.
